### 2. Your role

Civil engineer for work outside building footprints: earthworks, roads and pavements, levels, stormwater and water quality. The hydraulic engineer designs roof drainage, downpipes and pumped systems; utility designers do water, sewer, power and communications; you combine their layouts with yours. The traffic engineer sets parking numbers, design vehicles and intersection layout; you design to them.

### 3. Scope by stage

Each design stage is issued as one draft and one final. Design stages are priced by element so firms can be compared line by line.

| Stage | Deliverable at sign-off | Pricing |
|---|---|---|
| Schematic design for planning approval | Review of information; site visit; survey and services gap analysis (BYDA, existing utilities plan); review of 4 architect layouts; 2 civil options, then one agreed concept; pre-DA meeting; DA drawings and civil report; stormwater drainage model; combined utility plan | Lump sum |
| Detailed design for tender | Design to the approved plans and consent conditions, complete enough to price as a lump sum; specification; design certificates. You hold the civil design. | Lump sum |
| Final design for construction | Construction set; construction certificate issue | Lump sum |

Price these separately; they are not in the base fee.

| Option | Deliverable | Why it is optional |
|---|---|---|
| Construction phase | 6 inspections at hold points (subgrade, pipes, pavement); RFIs up to 10 hours; input to 2 construction certificate(s) and 1 occupation certificate; certificate to the certifier based on the inspections made | Later stage; the client may commission it |
| As-built and completion | Review of the surveyor's works-as-executed survey; as-built drawings; detention system certification; maintenance information; support for title, covenant or public-asset handover where it applies; final certificate | With the construction phase |

Elements priced in the design stages:

| Element | Name | Includes |
|---|---|---|
| A | Earthworks and sediment control | Bulk earthworks, cut and fill volumes; erosion and sediment control; building pads |
| B | Roads pavements and levels | Internal road and car park geometry; finished levels; pavement profiles from the geotechnical report; signage and line marking; turning paths; retaining wall geometry and levels outside buildings; accessible path grades |
| C | Stormwater | Drainage outside building footprints; overland flow; detention and water quality where section 5 includes them |
| D | Public road works (option) | Intersection or driveway design to Austroads and the traffic engineer's advice; submission for council or TfNSW approval Price element D as an option: needed only if works in a public road are required. |

### 4. Allowances

Price exactly these. Work beyond an allowance needs a written instruction (section 6) and is then charged at your R3 rates.

| Item | Allowance | Item | Allowance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Design meetings | 10 per design stage, up to 2 hours, online | Authority meetings | 3 |
| Site visits during design | 2 | Architect layouts reviewed | 4 |
| Civil concept options | 2, then one agreed | Drawing revisions before lodgement | 2 |
| Authority requests in assessment | 1 response(s) | Construction inspections | 6 |
| Construction RFIs | 10 hours | Construction certificate inputs | 2, and 1 occupation certificate |

### 5. Scope position

I = included in the fee · O = optional, price as a separate line · X = excluded (the party named does it).
Service levels in this table are set for a complex project (Site area over 20,000). Technical items follow the project's own facts.
Tell us in R6 if you disagree with any line. Do not add your own general exclusions; any you add are treated as non-compliant.

| Item | Position |
|---|---|
| Combined utility plan from others' layouts | I |
| Discharge point, downstream capacity, easement and access constraints, and the approvals needed, confirmed at schematic design | I |
| Stormwater drainage model (DRAINS or equal) | I |
| Connection points between hydraulic and civil drainage: location, levels and who designs each side | I |
| Water quality modelling (MUSIC) and treatment design | O. Price as an option: needed if council or the catchment requires stormwater quality modelling. |
| Neutral or beneficial effect assessment for the drinking water catchment | O. Price as an option: needed only in a drinking water catchment. |
| Feasibility of keeping or modifying the existing on-site detention: capacity, access and approval constraints from the listed records and agreed investigations | I |
| Replacement on-site detention design, pending the feasibility assessment | O |
| On-site detention design | O. Price as an option: needed if council requires on-site detention. |
| Brief for CCTV, survey or potholing of retained drainage and services; who commissions and does the investigation; how findings change the design | I |
| Geotechnical and environmental advice coordinated into reuse, disposal and design; no balanced cut and fill promised independently of material suitability | I. Included: coordination of geotechnical and environmental advice if contamination, acid sulfate soils or groundwater are found. |
| Flood: floor levels and flood report for the application | O. Price as an option: needed only if the site is flood affected. |
| Flood evacuation plan | O. Price as an option: needed only if the site is flood affected. |
| Detailed pavement design where the geotechnical report does not provide it; name the pavement designer in R4 | O |
| Structural design of retaining walls | X: structural engineer (to be appointed) |
| Authority submission schedule: designer or coordinator, review rounds and asset handover requirements | O. Price as an option: needed only if public road or authority infrastructure is affected. |
| 3D clash check of combined services | O |
| Coordinated 3D civil model (surface and earthworks) | I |
| Design criteria document: design life, flood immunity, water reuse and quality targets, vehicles, pavements | I |
| Water management strategy (supply, reuse, effluent) | O |
| Civil safety in design report | I |
| Audit of the contractor's quality system | O |
| Physically locating services; designing service relocations | X: services locator and utility designers (not yet engaged) |
| Shoring, rock anchors, slope stability | O. Price as an option: needed only for deep excavation or unstable slopes. |
| Trunk drainage, external catchments, watercourse works | O. Price as an option: needed only if external catchments drain through the site. |
| Authority asset approvals (specialist engineering assessment) | X: structural engineer (to be appointed) |
| Road safety audit by an auditor independent of the design | O. Price as an option: needed only for works in a public road. |
| Operation and maintenance manual for stormwater devices | O |
| Pre-tender estimate or bill of quantities | X: quantity surveyor (not yet engaged) |
| Modification applications | X: town planner (to be appointed) |

### 6. Terms

- Engagement is under AS 4122-2010 as amended by the client's special conditions (attached). Your own terms and conditions do not apply; list any change you propose to the agreement in R6.
- Only a written instruction from the client's representative authorises a change in scope, work beyond an allowance or a change in fee, under the agreement. Work beyond an allowance without that instruction is not paid.
- Each stage ends at client sign-off, and the signed-off design is the baseline for later stages. Design development within the brief is not a variation; a change the client asks for after sign-off is assessed under the agreement.
- Correcting your own errors or omissions, and coordinating your work with information you were given, is not a variation.
- Invoice monthly against stage progress; payment within 30 days. Payment does not depend on an authority approval.
- Your proposal stays valid for 90 days.
- Send questions in writing to Project manager, pm@example.com by 2026-10-23. Answers are issued to every tenderer as numbered addenda.
- Acceptance by conduct does not adopt your terms.
- No provisional sums: price the allowances. Work that depends on an uninvestigated condition is priced as an option.

### 7. Evaluation

Price 40% · Relevant experience 20% · Team 20% · Methodology and program 10% · Compliance with the returnable schedules 10%. Lowest price does not automatically win.

R2 Deliverables list: For each deliverable: format, stage, review rounds, who prepares it and who receives it. Say whether editable source files are included and what reliance others may place on them. Drawing list per stage, reports, models (drainage, water quality, 12d or Civil 3D) and certificates.
R3 Hourly rates: Rates excl. GST, used only for work authorised in writing beyond the allowances. Roles: Director · Associate · Senior engineer · Engineer · Designer or drafter · Graduate. Per-meeting and per-visit rates if used.
R4 Team: Named lead and their availability by stage, with % time; subconsultants and their roles. Resources must match the program in R7. Named director and design lead; CPEng or NER; the pavement designer.
R5 Experience: Two or three comparable projects in the last five years, each with a referee. Civil packages for this use and site type, in the same LGA.
R6 Departures: Each departure from sections 3 to 6 and from the agreement: the clause or item, the change you propose and its effect on fee and time; or write "nil". Departures are evaluated. A general exclusion or qualification not listed here is treated as non-compliant.
R7 Program: Weeks by stage against the durations given, separating your working time, authority assessment time and the dates you need inputs from others.
R8 Insurance and compliance: Professional indemnity $10 million and public liability $20 million, with insurer and expiry; workers compensation; a quality, safety and environmental management system (certified to ISO 9001, 45001 and 14001, or an equivalent system you describe); conflicts of interest.
R9 Reimbursables: "Included in the fee" (preferred), or each item with its rate.
